title: The 1+1 Gap, Machine-Checked: Goldbach endpoints as consequences of binary Goldbach, and a kernel-checked circularity certificate for arXiv:2611.09007v1
description:
What is claimed. In Lean 4 with Mathlib, the three headline endpoints of the goldbach-lean development (Chen 1+2, Li–Liu 1+1.9, Wu 1+1.8938) are proved to be logical consequences of binary Goldbach (set the second multiplier to 1). Separately, Theorem 1.1 of arXiv:2611.09007v1 is formalized under the paper's own definition of big-O (a limit ratio equal to a nonzero constant), and is proved to imply binary Goldbach; the proof lists the current case G(2n) among the assumptions, which is circular, and separately takes positivity of G(2n-2) as an input that already presupposes the required positivity under the literal reading and lacks a basis under the standard reading.

What is not claimed. This does not prove the Goldbach conjecture. No unconditional theorem here concludes binary Goldbach. No independence result is proved (the witness theorems only show that the endpoint predicates admit objects that 1+1 forbids). No claim of being first is made: see the prior-art record in the package.

Evidence. Eight theorems plus one definitional check are replayed with leanchecker; axiom sets are contained in {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. Logs and an RFC 3161 timestamp over the manifest are included.

What is new in 0.1.3. Text-only corrections and evidence-list alignment, with no new mathematical claims: equations (1)--(2) are each off by one in opposite directions; circularity is restricted to the assumption of the current case G(2n), while G(2n-2)>0 is treated as a separate positivity-reading issue; and the endpoint-hierarchy and Wu rebuild status files are now bound by the sealed 79-file manifest. The gap-v0.1.2 seal remains unchanged.
notes: The prose in this package is released under CC BY 4.0; the Lean sources are Apache-2.0, matching the upstream goldbach-lean repository. Upstream files retain their original notices.
